PullRequest.Title: Do not forward request credentials across origins on redirects
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to the redirect credential-handling feedback on [microsoft/vscode#325804](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/325804). This is limited to the request service and its tests; it does not change marketplace authentication or token renewal.

## Changes

- Resolve relative and protocol-relative redirect locations once, then compare normalized origins and request that exact resolved HTTP(S) URL. Invalid and non-HTTP(S) targets remain unfollowed.
- On any scheme, host, or effective-port change, remove case-insensitive `Authorization`, `Cookie`, and `Cookie2` headers and explicit basic credentials. Preserve same-origin authentication, proxy authorization, and other headers. Credentials stay removed if a later redirect returns to the original origin.
- Explicitly use Electron's manual redirect mode and handle its separate `redirect` event. Its default automatic redirect behavior bypasses the Node response callback. Fresh requests now apply the policy and redirect budget on every hop, while preserving cancellation and Chromium's method/body changes.

Node coverage includes scheme/port changes, default-port equivalence, mixed-case headers, resolved destinations, basic authentication, A-to-B-to-A chains, invalid targets, limits, and cancellation. Electron coverage uses real `net.request` calls to two loopback origins rather than assuming Chromium has the same existing credential behavior as Node.

## Validation

Run on Windows against upstream `8159c00b2e71eedd1abffcaac36cc3582785ca06`, using Electron 43.7.7.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node .\build\npm\electronTypes.ts` | Passed; generated checksum-verified Electron declarations. |
| `npm run typecheck-client` | Passed; native TypeScript 7.0.2, zero errors. |
| `node .\build\next\build-fast.ts --client-only` | Passed; cold client build and final incremental refresh. |
| `npm run valid-layers-check` | Passed. |
| `npm run precommit` | Passed for all four staged files. |
| `node --check .\test\unit\electron\index.js` | Passed. |
| `git --no-pager diff --cached --check` | Passed. |

Focused test command: **40 passed**, including all 32 new redirect cases and the eight existing retry/cancellation cases.

```powershell
$env:VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH='1'
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\request\test\node\requestService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\request\test\electron-main\requestService.test.ts --grep 'Request Service(?! Kerberos lookup)'
```

**Existing environment limitation:** the unfiltered command below reports **41 passed, one failed** because the unchanged `Kerberos lookup` test cannot resolve the `kerberos` module in this checkout's Electron renderer. The same failure was reproduced with the unmodified upstream request service; no redirect tests are excluded.

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\request\test\node\requestService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\request\test\electron-main\requestService.test.ts
```

Regression confirmation: temporarily transpiling only the upstream request service into this worktree's generated output and running the command below produces **four expected failures**: Node host-change credential forwarding, Node port-change credential forwarding, Electron ignoring a zero redirect limit, and the unchanged Kerberos limitation. The patched output was restored byte-for-byte, then the 40-case focused command passed again.

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\request\test\node\requestService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\request\test\electron-main\requestService.test.ts --grep 'Kerberos lookup|redirects host change|redirects port change|Electron redirects honors a redirect limit of 0'
```

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Manual redirect mode, recursive request creation, timer setup per request, the redirect limit, and timed desktop callers are explicit in the changed and surrounding code.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The effective timeout grows linearly with followed redirects, up to four timeout periods with the default redirect limit.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Electron followed redirects on one ClientRequest, so one timeout timer bounded the complete redirect chain.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Electron redirects now abort the current request and create a new request that receives a fresh full-duration timeout.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added manual redirect mode at line 258 replaces Electron's single automatically redirecting ClientRequest with the new per-hop request recursion.
Findings.Title: Preserve one timeout budget across redirects
Findings.Impact: A slow redirect chain can leave extension gallery requests pending for multiple 60-second periods rather than the configured single period.
Findings.Evidence: The Electron service always sets isChromiumNetwork. Each nodeRequestAttempt arms setTimeout(options.timeout), and the new redirect handler recursively invokes nodeRequest for every hop. Gallery asset calls set a default 60000 ms timeout.
Findings.Recommendation: Carry the initial absolute deadline or remaining timeout through recursive redirects.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop Electron request that follows one or more HTTP redirects, including extension gallery asset and metadata requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every redirect response and the final response must complete before the caller receives an IRequestContext. Timed extension gallery requests are directly blocked on this chain.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue the next HTTP(S) request after an Electron redirect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential network request per redirect target, capped at four total requests under the default limit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Chromium automatic redirect handling already issued one HTTP request per target, but all hops stayed within one ClientRequest and one timeout timer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All hops are on the caller's critical path. Each newly created hop now receives a fresh full timeout, so cumulative wait can exceed the logical request's configured bound.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Proxy desktop request options to the shared/main process and return the fully buffered response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request and one buffered IPC response per logical request, independent of redirect count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single IPC round trip wrapped the automatically followed redirect chain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The IPC waits for the entire redirect chain and therefore exposes the increased timeout latency to renderer callers.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Redirect count after validation, capped at three followed redirects by default (four HTTP requests total).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Redirects are strictly sequential. The new handler aborts one Electron ClientRequest before recursively starting the next; there is no parallel fan-out or shared limiter involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Electron's Chromium HTTP cache remains enabled unless disableCache is set, and each target URL uses the existing session cache. No request coalescing is present. The diff does not change cache keys, but a cache hit does not prevent the per-hop timeout budget from being reset when a redirect is processed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: manual redirect mode, abort, recursive request creation, and per-attempt timer setup are explicit, and a real 60-second desktop caller is traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most redirects are fast, so typical added latency may be small; slow CDN/proxy chains or degraded networks can consume multiple timeout windows, up to nearly four minutes for a 60-second gallery timeout.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable latency regression: the diff resets the configured timeout at each redirect rather than preserving the original deadline.

Scenarios.Scenario: Node transport request that follows HTTP redirects
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each sequential redirect hop and the final response are required before nodeRequest resolves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per redirect hop, at most four total by default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Node path already recursively issued one network request per followed redirect; the diff normalizes targets, strips credentials, and drains redirect responses without increasing hop count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All hops remain on the critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Validated HTTP(S) redirect count, capped at three followed redirects by default.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One request at a time; recursive redirect handling was already sequential before the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: This layer has no response cache or coalescing. The existing agent may reuse connections. Header cloning occurs only after a cross-origin redirect and is bounded by request header count and redirect limit.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the before/after diff preserves recursive Node network cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Header counts and redirect chains are normally small and hard-bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional Node performance regression. URL parsing and bounded header filtering are negligible relative to the existing network hop, and res.resume improves response cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Direct response, invalid/non-HTTP redirect, or exhausted redirect budget
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A single network response completes the request; invalid targets and redirects at the limit are returned without another hop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue the initial HTTP request and return its response when no valid redirect is followed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Direct responses already used one request. The diff adds only constant redirect-policy checks and an event listener.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The one response is the critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One logical request and no followed redirect.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing Node/Chromium cache behavior is unchanged; disableCache still maps to no-store.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; added CPU/allocation is bounded constant work per response.

Scenarios.Scenario: Electron redirect integration tests through the new vscode:test-platform-request handler
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each test performs one IPC invoke, dynamically loads three already-built modules in the main process, runs one to four loopback HTTP requests, then buffers the final response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive each renderer test invocation and return its result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC call per test request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This test-only IPC route did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the test critical path only; absent from product workflows outside the test harness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exercise real Electron net.request redirects against two loopback servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One to four local requests per test case.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These loopback redirect tests did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Test execution waits for these local requests; no shipped user workflow is affected.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed test case count and redirect loops capped by test inputs/default limit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The three module imports are parallel; redirect network requests are sequential. Test cases run under the existing test runner scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ES module imports are cached after first load. Loopback responses are not product cache inputs.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Test-suite duration impact is small and bounded; module imports are cached.
Scenarios.Verdict: No product performance finding; added work is test-only and bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and the redirect call paths for Node and Electron. One medium-confidence-impact, high-mechanism-confidence latency issue was submitted: recursive Electron redirects reset the full timeout on every hop. Network cardinality otherwise remains bounded and unchanged, cleanup is improved for Node redirect bodies, and test-only IPC/network additions are bounded.
